message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff. Pebble Spring spent countless hours observing the builders at work, taking careful notes in a small leather journal. The mortar mixed with river clay seemed to stick better when a drop of sap was added. Each morning, the young Leshy woke before the sun to gather stones from the nearby stream. Their branches grew longer and stronger, reaching up toward the sky in longing. A kind mason named Aldric noticed the curious creature and offered a gentle smile. Over time, Pebble Spring's understanding of foundations and load-bearing walls deepened considerably. The arcane magic in the staff allowed the stones to be lifted without the need for ropes. Neighbors whispered about the strange green figure they saw working among the mortar and dust. Pebble Spring did not mind the whispers, for the joy of creation filled every hollow of their wooden heart. By the third month, the first modest cottage was taking shape behind the old oak grove. The roof needed thatching, and Pebble Spring learned to weave reeds with surprising dexterity. Aldric praised the work, noting that the joints were sealed tighter than most human masons could manage. The Leshy's roots had begun to intertwine with the foundation stones, giving the structure an unusual resilience. Rain came that autumn, and the new cottage stood firm while several older ones leaked badly. Word spread through the village that the mysterious builder had a gift for making walls that breathed. Pebble Spring felt proud, though pride was an unfamiliar emotion for one made of earth and leaf. The staff glowed faintly each night, humming with a low melodic resonance that soothed the surrounding trees. Winter arrived, and the Leshy tucked away their long limbs beneath a blanket of fallen leaves. When spring returned, Pebble Spring emerged refreshed and ready to begin yet another grand project. Although the very first attempt at building a tall tower in the village had resulted in a rather uneven and wobbly structure that leaned dangerously to one side in the strong autumn wind, the spotty pattern of cracks reminded Pebble Spring of dappled sunlight filtering through ancient forest canopy.
